class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  JOIN_TABLES = {
    "tag_ids" => { table: "filters_tags", foreign_key: "tag_id" },
    "board_ids" => { table: "boards_filters", foreign_key: "board_id" },
    "assignee_ids" => { table: "assignees_filters", foreign_key: "assignee_id" },
    "creator_ids" => { table: "creators_filters", foreign_key: "creator_id" },
    "closer_ids" => { table: "closers_filters", foreign_key: "closer_id" }
  }.freeze

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::Filter)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::Filter.where(account_id: account.id).includes(:tags, :boards, :assignees, :creators, :closers)
    end

    def serialize_record(filter)
      super.merge(
        "tag_ids" => filter.tags.map(&:id),
        "board_ids" => filter.attributes_before_type_cast["id"] ? load_raw_board_ids(filter.id) : [],
        "assignee_ids" => filter.assignees.map(&:id),
        "creator_ids" => filter.creators.map(&:id),
        "closer_ids" => filter.closers.map(&:id)
      )
    end

    def load_raw_board_ids(filter_id)
      raw_id = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.serialize(filter_id)
      ApplicationRecord.connection.select_values(
        ApplicationRecord.sanitize_sql_array([ "SELECT board_id FROM boards_filters WHERE filter_id = ?", raw_id ])
      ).map { |val| ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new.deserialize(val) }
    end

    def import_records(mapper)
      imported_filter_ids = []

      each_exported_batch do |batch, _path|
        join_rows_by_table = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = [] }

        transformed = batch.map do |raw_attrs|
          attrs = raw_attrs.deep_dup
          associations = attrs.extract!(*JOIN_TABLES.keys)
          remapped = transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
          filter_id = remapped["id"]
          imported_filter_ids << filter_id

          JOIN_TABLES.each do |assoc_key, config|
            Array(associations[assoc_key]).each do |target_id|
              join_rows_by_table[config[:table]] << {
                "filter_id" => filter_id,
                config[:foreign_key] => mapper.remap_id(target_id)
              }
            end
          end

          # Temporary unique digest before recomputing after HABTM rows are inserted
          remapped["params_digest"] = Digest::MD5.hexdigest("#{filter_id}:#{remapped["params_digest"]}")
          remapped
        end

        ::Filter.insert_all!(transformed) if transformed.any?
        insert_join_rows(join_rows_by_table)
      end

      refresh_params_digests(imported_filter_ids) if imported_filter_ids.any?
    end

    def transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
      remapped = super

      if remapped["fields"].is_a?(Hash)
        fields = remapped["fields"].deep_dup
        if fields["card_ids"].is_a?(Array)
          fields["card_ids"] = fields["card_ids"].map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
        end
        if fields["column_ids"].is_a?(Array)
          fields["column_ids"] = fields["column_ids"].map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
        end
        remapped["fields"] = fields
      end

      remapped
    end

    def insert_join_rows(join_rows_by_table)
      uuid_type = ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.new

      join_rows_by_table.each do |table_name, rows|
        next if rows.empty?

        rows.each do |row|
          columns = row.keys
          placeholders = columns.map { "?" }.join(", ")
          values = columns.map { |col| uuid_type.serialize(row[col]) }
          sql = ApplicationRecord.sanitize_sql_array([
            "INSERT INTO #{table_name} (#{columns.join(", ")}) VALUES (#{placeholders})",
            *values
          ])
          ApplicationRecord.connection.execute(sql)
        end
      end
    end

    def refresh_params_digests(filter_ids)
      ::Filter.where(id: filter_ids).find_each do |filter|
        filter.update_column(:params_digest, ::Filter.digest_params(filter.as_params))
      rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
        filter.destroy!
      end
    end
end
EOF

          blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
        end
      end
    end

    def check_records
      each_blob_record do |blob_attrs|
        storage_path = "storage/#{blob_attrs["key"]}"
        unless zip.exists?(storage_path)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::Error, "The archive is missing an attached file (#{blob_attrs["filename"]})."
        end

        expected_size = blob_attrs["byte_size"].to_i
        actual_size = zip.entry_size(storage_path)
        if expected_size != actual_size
          raise Account::DataTransfer::Error, "The attached file #{blob_attrs["filename"]} in the archive is incomplete or corrupted."
        end
      end
    end

      service = ::ActiveStorage::Blob.service

        old_key = blob_attrs["key"]
        new_key = mapper.remap_token(old_key, namespace: "blob", length: 28)
        mapper.uploaded_keys << new_key

        zip.open_file("storage/#{old_key}") do |entry_io|
          service.upload(
            new_key,
            entry_io,
            content_type: blob_attrs["content_type"],
            filename: ::ActiveStorage::Filename.new(blob_attrs["filename"].to_s)
          )
        end

class Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActionText::RichText)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActionText::RichText.where(account: account)
    end

    def serialize_record(record)
      super.merge("body" => convert_sgids_to_gids(record.body&.to_html.to_s))
    end

    def transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
      remapped = super
      remapped["body"] = convert_gids_to_sgids(attrs["body"].to_s, mapper)
      remapped
    end

    def convert_sgids_to_gids(html)
      return html if html.blank?

      fragment = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(html)

      fragment.css("action-text-attachment[sgid]").each do |node|
        if parsed = SignedGlobalID.parse(node["sgid"], for: ::ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME)
          gid = URI::GID.build(app: GlobalID.app, model_name: parsed.model_name, model_id: parsed.model_id).to_s
          node["gid"] = gid
          node.remove_attribute("sgid")
          node.remove_attribute("url") if parsed.model_name == "ActiveStorage::Blob"
        end
      end

      fragment.to_html
    end

    def convert_gids_to_sgids(html, mapper)
      return html if html.blank?

      fragment = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(html)

      fragment.css("action-text-attachment[gid]").each do |node|
        parsed_gid = URI::GID.parse(node["gid"])
        node.remove_attribute("gid")
        new_id = mapper.remap_id(parsed_gid.model_id)

        if attachable = find_attachable(parsed_gid.model_name, new_id)
          node["sgid"] = attachable.attachable_sgid
          if attachable.is_a?(::ActiveStorage::Blob)
            node["url"] = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.polymorphic_url(
              attachable,
              only_path: true,
              script_name: account.slug
            )
          end
        end
      rescue URI::InvalidURIError
        node.remove_attribute("gid")
      end

      rewrite_internal_links(fragment, mapper)
      fragment.to_html
    end

    def find_attachable(model_name, id)
      case model_name
      when "ActiveStorage::Blob"
        ::ActiveStorage::Blob.find_by(id: id, account_id: account.id)
      when "User"
        ::User.find_by(id: id, account_id: account.id)
      when "Card"
        ::Card.find_by(id: id, account_id: account.id)
      end
    end

    def rewrite_internal_links(fragment, mapper)
      old_slug = mapper.old_account_slug
      return if old_slug.blank?

      fragment.css("a[href]").each do |link|
        href = link["href"].to_s
        if href == old_slug || href.start_with?("#{old_slug}/")
          link["href"] = href.sub(/\A#{Regexp.escape(old_slug)}/, account.slug)
        end
      end
    end
end
EOF

**The Binary Blob Blunder**

Aha! It finally clicked! `imported_filter` was indeed nil, and now I understand why! It all comes down to how we're handling binary data in our SQL queries. Let's trace it back.

I was looking at `FilterRecordSet#records` where it fetches the filters: `::Filter.where(account_id: account.id).includes(:tags, :boards, :assignees, :creators, :closers)`. Then I was reviewing `RecordSet#each_record_batch` and `Filter::Resources#boards`. The `includes(:boards)` was calling `Filter#boards`, and I was suspicious of how that was interacting with the `Filter.where(account: target_account)` query.

Then I jumped to `FilterRecordSet#insert_join_rows`, where we're constructing SQL queries. That's where I saw it: `sanitize_sql_array` is quoting `Binary::Data` as a string literal (e.g., `'0190...'`) in the SQL statement, which is incorrect for SQLite! SQLite expects binary blobs to be represented as `X'0190...'`. This isn't the same as the way `exec_query` works with bind parameters, which handles `Binary::Data` correctly as a `SQLite3::Blob`. The same issue was showing up in `load_raw_board_ids` as well.

The tests saved us! Using `exec_query` with bind parameters (or ActiveRecord's HABTM methods or even `Arel`) works perfectly. This is also how `filter.tag_ids = ...` functions internally.

My breakthrough: we need to bypass our custom logic and lean on ActiveRecord's native association methods, which correctly handle binary data on both SQLite and MySQL without these raw SQL quoting issues.

So, for the export, I will use `filter.association(:boards).scope.pluck(:id)` to fetch the board IDs. Then, during import, after the `Filter.insert_all!` step, I'll load the filters and use ActiveRecord's HABTM setters like `filter.tags = Tag.where(id: remapped_tag_ids)` — it's database agnostic and uses ActiveRecord's internal UUID type casting and avoids any raw SQL.

I'm going to test this immediately to confirm that it works!

class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  ASSOCIATION_MODELS = {
    "tag_ids" => { assoc: :tags, model: ::Tag },
    "board_ids" => { assoc: :boards, model: ::Board },
    "assignee_ids" => { assoc: :assignees, model: ::User },
    "creator_ids" => { assoc: :creators, model: ::User },
    "closer_ids" => { assoc: :closers, model: ::User }
  }.freeze

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::Filter)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::Filter.where(account_id: account.id).includes(:tags, :assignees, :creators, :closers)
    end

    def serialize_record(filter)
      super.merge(
        "tag_ids" => filter.tags.map(&:id),
        "board_ids" => filter.association(:boards).scope.pluck(:id),
        "assignee_ids" => filter.assignees.map(&:id),
        "creator_ids" => filter.creators.map(&:id),
        "closer_ids" => filter.closers.map(&:id)
      )
    end

    def import_records(mapper)
      each_exported_batch do |batch, _path|
        associations_by_filter_id = {}

        transformed = batch.map do |raw_attrs|
          attrs = raw_attrs.deep_dup
          associations = attrs.extract!(*ASSOCIATION_MODELS.keys)
          remapped = transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
          filter_id = remapped["id"]
          associations_by_filter_id[filter_id] = associations

          remapped["params_digest"] = Digest::MD5.hexdigest("#{filter_id}:#{remapped["params_digest"]}")
          remapped
        end

        ::Filter.insert_all!(transformed) if transformed.any?
        restore_filter_associations(associations_by_filter_id, mapper)
      end
    end

    def transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
      remapped = super

      if remapped["fields"].is_a?(Hash)
        fields = remapped["fields"].deep_dup
        if fields["card_ids"].is_a?(Array)
          fields["card_ids"] = fields["card_ids"].map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
        end
        if fields["column_ids"].is_a?(Array)
          fields["column_ids"] = fields["column_ids"].map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
        end
        remapped["fields"] = fields
      end

      remapped
    end

    def restore_filter_associations(associations_by_filter_id, mapper)
      ::Filter.where(id: associations_by_filter_id.keys).find_each do |filter|
        associations = associations_by_filter_id.fetch(filter.id, {})

        ASSOCIATION_MODELS.each do |key, config|
          remapped_ids = Array(associations[key]).filter_map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
          if remapped_ids.any?
            records = config[:model].where(id: remapped_ids).to_a
            filter.association(config[:assoc]).replace(records)
          end
        end

        filter.instance_variable_set(:@boards, nil)
        filter.instance_variable_set(:@as_params, nil)
        filter.update_column(:params_digest, ::Filter.digest_params(filter.as_params))
      rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
        filter.destroy!
      end
    end
end
EOF

messages.thinking:
**Eureka! Unraveling the Database Conundrum**

Okay, here's what's hitting me. I was looking at this ZIP file, and boom! The `data/filters` directory wasn't present at all. That immediately got me thinking about how Rails 8 handles HABTM associations when combined with `.in_batches`. I know from experience that `.includes(:tags, :assignees, :creators, :closers).in_batches` is the culprit. In Rails 8, when HABTM is involved, `.in_batches` introduces a `WHERE id IN (...)` clause, while `.includes` resorts to either `eager_load` (a `LEFT OUTER JOIN`) or `preload`. It's all about how these joins interact.

I started digging into the specifics and realized that `.preload(:tags, :assignees, :creators, :closers)` is the more appropriate solution here, not `.includes`. The critical point is avoiding that `LEFT OUTER JOIN`. That was the source of my problem, so calling `.preload` is the right choice (NOT `.includes`, or calling `.preload` INSIDE `each_record_batch` on `Filter.where(account_id: account.id)`!).

The real head-scratcher was why `Filter.where(account_id: account.id).includes(...).in_batches` was yielding zero rows. It finally hit me: `in_batches` internally executes `pluck(:id)` on the result of `Filter.where(account_id: account.id).includes(...)`. This becomes a mess when `.includes` defaults to a `LEFT OUTER JOIN` on `assignees_filters`, `creators_filters`, and `closers_filters` which each join the `users` table three times! That’s where the problems start.

The fix, it seems, is `FilterRecordSet#records`, which will be as simple as `::Filter.where(account_id: account.id).preload(:tags, :assignees, :creators, :closers)`. This means NO `LEFT OUTER JOIN` ever. The use of `preload` will always use separate `SELECT ... WHERE filter_id IN (...)` queries after `in_batches` loads the initial batch of `Filter` rows.

Time to test this out with `.preload` right away! I know this will be an invaluable test to write.

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/account/data_transfer/filter_record_set.rb
class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  ASSOCIATION_MODELS = {
    "tag_ids" => { assoc: :tags, model: ::Tag },
    "board_ids" => { assoc: :boards, model: ::Board },
    "assignee_ids" => { assoc: :assignees, model: ::User },
    "creator_ids" => { assoc: :creators, model: ::User },
    "closer_ids" => { assoc: :closers, model: ::User }
  }.freeze

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::Filter)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::Filter.where(account_id: account.id).preload(:tags, :assignees, :creators, :closers)
    end

    def serialize_record(filter)
      super.merge(
        "tag_ids" => filter.tags.map(&:id),
        "board_ids" => filter.association(:boards).scope.pluck(:id),
        "assignee_ids" => filter.assignees.map(&:id),
        "creator_ids" => filter.creators.map(&:id),
        "closer_ids" => filter.closers.map(&:id)
      )
    end

    def import_records(mapper)
      each_exported_batch do |batch, _path|
        associations_by_filter_id = {}

        transformed = batch.map do |raw_attrs|
          attrs = raw_attrs.deep_dup
          associations = attrs.extract!(*ASSOCIATION_MODELS.keys)
          remapped = transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
          filter_id = remapped["id"]
          associations_by_filter_id[filter_id] = associations

          remapped["params_digest"] = Digest::MD5.hexdigest("#{filter_id}:#{remapped["params_digest"]}")
          remapped
        end

        ::Filter.insert_all!(transformed) if transformed.any?
        restore_filter_associations(associations_by_filter_id, mapper)
      end
    end

    def transform_record_for_import(attrs, mapper)
      remapped = super

      if remapped["fields"].is_a?(Hash)
        fields = remapped["fields"].deep_dup
        if fields["card_ids"].is_a?(Array)
          fields["card_ids"] = fields["card_ids"].map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
        end
        if fields["column_ids"].is_a?(Array)
          fields["column_ids"] = fields["column_ids"].map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
        end
        remapped["fields"] = fields
      end

      remapped
    end

    def restore_filter_associations(associations_by_filter_id, mapper)
      ::Filter.where(id: associations_by_filter_id.keys).find_each do |filter|
        associations = associations_by_filter_id.fetch(filter.id, {})

        ASSOCIATION_MODELS.each do |key, config|
          remapped_ids = Array(associations[key]).filter_map { |id| mapper.remap_id(id) }
          if remapped_ids.any?
            records = config[:model].where(id: remapped_ids).to_a
            filter.association(config[:assoc]).replace(records)
          end
        end

        filter.instance_variable_set(:@boards, nil)
        filter.instance_variable_set(:@as_params, nil)
        filter.update_column(:params_digest, ::Filter.digest_params(filter.as_params))
      rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
        filter.destroy!
      end
    end
end
EOF

First, the `Export` model. It handles the basic export process with a built-in expiration (`EXPIRATION_TIME = 1.day`), and I'm really liking the `after_create_commit :build_later` which triggers a job. The `build_now` method wraps everything in `Current.with_account`, which is essential for ensuring correct account context even in tests. This is clean and smart. The `accessible_to?` method is well-defined.

Now, `Export::BuildJob` is simple, just calling `build_now` on the export object.

`Account::Export` and `User::DataExport` are extensions. `Account::Export`'s `accessible_to?` implementation is solid, and the `download_url` generation is good. I need to be careful with `ZipFile.create_for` here, making sure it plays nicely with any file handling I might have.

`User::DataExport` is where it gets interesting, with its data export logic. I'm especially interested in the zero-N+1 preloading in `export_cards_to`. I need to review this preloading strategy. It seems incredibly efficient. The use of per-card `blob_paths` to avoid duplicate file additions to the ZIP is excellent, and the JSON creation appears well-structured. It's properly using `blob.download` and I like the use of relative paths for image attachments.

Now the real complexity is in `Account::Import`. I'm going to take notes here:
1.  We have the `Account::Import.start!` method. *Critical* to note here: We're running in `Current.without_account`, which ensures the job gets enqueued without an account. Then, when `file.attach` is called, it happens within `Current.with_account`, so ActiveStorage has the right account. Nice!
2.  `process_now`:  I need to go line by line through this.
    *   The `ApplicationRecord.transaction` with `requires_new: true` is good to see; this is an all-or-nothing operation.
    *   `mapper = Account::DataTransfer::IdMapper.new(account)` *before* `ZipFile.read_from` is a fantastic catch. This ensures any uploaded files can be deleted if an error occurs later, even if the transaction fails mid-process.
    *   `ensure_importer_access` carefully handles user creation, and I appreciate the logic to grant access to existing boards *before* `after_create_commit` fires – this prevents a race condition, and it's perfect to use `Access.insert_all` because it avoids any collisions. I need to test all these edge cases!
    *   `reindex_search` is pretty standard, but important.
    *   `reconcile_imported_storage` is smart, making a storage `entry` and a total for every board and the account.
3.  **Error Handling**: I need to pay *very* close attention to `cleanup_failed_import`. This ensures that any uploaded files are deleted (`mapper&.uploaded_keys`), the import `.zip` is purged, the import record's `account` is set to `nil`, failure is recorded, and the failed account is destroyed (with all associated data). This is a *very* comprehensive cleanup. I need to test this *very* carefully! I love how `Storage::Entry.suppressing_recording` is used and then run `purge_residual_account_records(failed_account.id)` to be *completely* sure all related records are wiped.
4.  **Success Cleanup**: `purge_uploaded_archive` ensures the .zip file is purged *after* a successful import.
5.  All the mailers are solid: the exports clearly state download expiration and the imports clearly explain any failure, with links to retry.

In short: the design seems very thorough, especially the error handling and data cleanup, but I *must* test it thoroughly with different scenarios. I'm happy with this, let's get building!

**Reviewing the Data Export and Import Implementation**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. First, I need to make sure the data model is sound. Looking at the `Account` model, I see the `exports` table cleverly stores both `Account::Export` and `User::DataExport` records using `account_id` as the foreign key. This allows for clear associations: `Account` has many `exports` (both `Account::Export` and `User::DataExport`), and also, since an account `has_many :users`, when an account is destroyed, its users are also destroyed, and their associated data exports are cleaned up. On `Account`, `has_many :exports, class_name: "Account::Export", dependent: :destroy` and `has_many :all_exports, class_name: "Export", dependent: :destroy`.

Now, let's move onto the routes, controllers, and views.

Starting with `config/routes.rb`, I've got to carefully consider the different access points. Under `namespace :account`, there are the resources for settings, cancellation, entropy, exports, imports, and join code. Separately, for each user, there's `resources :users`, and within that, nested routes for `data_exports`, avatar, role, events, push subscriptions, and so on.

Next, I need to analyze the controllers and views, ensuring everything is locked down securely.

*   **`Account::ExportsController`**: Admin-only, of course, with `before_action :ensure_admin`. It manages exports initiated by admins. The `create` action sets up an `Account::Export` and handles the response. The `show` action provides the download if the export is valid (within a day, and initiated by the current admin), otherwise, it renders an expired view with HTTP status `410 Gone`. Important: the `set_export` method ensures that only the admin who initiated the export can view it. This is important to consider. First, the **Account Export**. We're talking permissions, file generation, job queueing, email delivery, download links (with expiration!), and making sure other users can't access each other's exports. The tests need to confirm admin/non-admin behavior on both the controller and the model. I'm focusing on those 403s and 410s and ensuring that expired links actually *are* expired. The .zip creation itself needs to be verified as well.

Next, the **User/Profile Export**. This is very similar in structure, but permissions are now user-specific. The content of the .zip file is *critical* here. It has to only include cards and associated data that the requesting user can actually *see*. I'm thinking about the logic around filtering published cards, excluding drafts, and excluding private boards. The testing must include a meticulous examination of the included JSON, and making sure all attachments are present and *correct*.

Then comes the **Account Import**. This is where things get really complex. We're not just moving data, we're recreating a whole account! I want to confirm that non-signed in users get redirected to sign in, and that the import succeeds for both existing and new users. We *must* verify a complete round-trip (export-import) to ensure the integrity of the data. I'm imagining a full test case with *everything* – multiple boards, different user roles, varied content, attachments galore. A new account needs to be created on import, with no changes to the source account. The import also needs to verify that the data is *actually* imported: the boards, the people, the files, the searchability. I'm also planning the important failure tests. Uploading a bad file, the wrong file, or running into errors *during* the import process. I'm visualizing the tests needed to confirm that in each of these cases, the import rolls back completely, leaving *nothing* behind. Every record needs to be clean, and storage needs to be purged.

We also have to test **S3 Streaming**. This one is straightforward: verify that the streaming functionality works if `aws-sdk-s3` is installed.

Finally, we have the **Mailer Tests**. We want to test the email contents - HTML and text parts, recipients, subjects, download links, expiration notice, failure reason.

I want tests for *everything*, from permissions to data integrity, error handling, and expiration logic. I see a lot of integration tests in my future.

**Debugging Test Failures**

Okay, so 15 out of the 17 tests passed immediately – that's a good start. Let's dig into those two failures; it seems like they're test setup issues.

The first one, the `Vips::Error: VipsForeignLoad`, is a classic. It looks like ActionText's `process: :immediately` for image content types is biting me. The test was providing what it *thought* was a JPEG ("second moon image") but the underlying bytes weren't actually valid JPEG. That's because the test was supplying image data with the wrong header. The fix is to provide proper image bytes, so I'll try using `File.open(file_fixture("avatar.png"), "rb")` with the right filename and content type – something like `"moon.jpg"` and `"image/png"`. That should give us the correct image data.

The second failure in `Account::ExportsControllerTest` is more intriguing. The `logout_and_sign_in_as :david` helper seems to be the culprit. The error is that after that call, `get account_settings_path` is redirecting to the login page.  The test helper deletes all `Sessions`, and calls `sign_in_as identity`. The test helper calls `Session.delete_all`, and `sign_in_as` tries to login with `post session_path`. The issue appears to be that the test helper deletes the session but when `post session_path` gets hit, the old `session_token` cookie is still there, and the `resume_session` function gives back `nil`. When `get account_settings_path` is hit, it redirects to `/session/new`. The fix is to call the `delete session_path` properly. The fix looks to be in `SessionTestHelper`: `cookies.delete :session_token` which effectively calls `session_token=""` on the test server. The test is calling `logout_and_sign_in_as :david` BEFORE the first `get` call, so the session is being cleared too early, or incorrectly.

So, to solve this: I need to fix the session cleanup in the test helpers – calling `delete session_path` directly seems like the right approach.

I'll make these changes directly in the test files now, both of the tests that I have identified. And then I'll rerun all 17 tests to verify that these fixes resolve both issues. Hopefully, everything will pass this time.

class ZipFileS3Test < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "create_for and read_from work with S3Service" do
    require "active_storage/service/s3_service"

    s3_service = ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service.new(
      bucket: "fizzy-test-bucket",
      region: "us-east-1",
      access_key_id: "test-key",
      secret_access_key: "test-secret",
      endpoint: "https://s3.example.com",
      force_path_style: true
    )

    uploaded_objects = {}

    # Stub S3 multipart / single-part upload_stream to capture streamed bytes in memory
    s3_service.define_singleton_method(:upload_stream) do |key:, **, &block|
      buf = StringIO.new("".b)
      block.call(buf)
      uploaded_objects[key] = buf.string
    end

    # Stub HTTP Range GET requests for ZipFile::RemoteIO against the presigned S3 URL
    stub_request(:get, %r{\Ahttps://s3\.example\.com/fizzy-test-bucket/}).to_return do |request|
      key = request.uri.path.delete_prefix("/fizzy-test-bucket/")
      bytes = uploaded_objects.fetch(key)
      range_header = request.headers["Range"]

      if range_header =~ /bytes=(\d+)-(\d+)/
        first, last = $1.to_i, $2.to_i
        slice = bytes.byteslice(first..last)
        {
          status: 206,
          body: slice,
          headers: {
            "Content-Range" => "bytes #{first}-#{first + slice.bytesize - 1}/#{bytes.bytesize}",
            "Content-Length" => slice.bytesize.to_s
          }
        }
      else
        { status: 200, body: bytes, headers: { "Content-Length" => bytes.bytesize.to_s } }
      end
    end

    services = ActiveStorage::Blob.services
    original_default = ActiveStorage::Blob.service
    services.instance_variable_get(:@configurations)[:s3_test] = {}
    services.instance_variable_get(:@services)[:s3_test] = s3_service
    s3_service.name = :s3_test
    ActiveStorage::Blob.service = s3_service

    export = Export.new(account: accounts("37s"), user: users(:kevin), type: "Account::Export")
    export.save!(validate: false)

    Current.with_account(accounts("37s")) do
      ZipFile.create_for(export.file, filename: "s3-export.zip") do |zip|
        zip.add_file("data/hello.json", '{"s3":true}')
      end
    end

    assert export.file.attached?
    assert_operator export.file.blob.byte_size, :>, 0

    ZipFile.read_from(export.file) do |reader|
      assert reader.exists?("data/hello.json")
      assert_equal '{"s3":true}', reader.read("data/hello.json")
    end
  ensure
    ActiveStorage::Blob.service = original_default if original_default
    services&.instance_variable_get(:@services)&.delete(:s3_test)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class ExportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "cleanup destroys expired exports and keeps current ones" do
    account = accounts("37s")
    admin = users(:kevin)

    fresh_export = account.exports.create!(user: admin)
    fresh_export.build_now

    expired_export = account.exports.create!(user: admin)
    expired_export.build_now
    expired_export.update_column(:completed_at, 25.hours.ago)

    abandoned_export = account.exports.create!(user: admin)
    abandoned_export.update_columns(status: "failed", created_at: 3.days.ago)

    Export.cleanup

    assert Export.exists?(fresh_export.id)
    assert_not Export.exists?(expired_export.id)
    assert_not Export.exists?(abandoned_export.id)
  end

  test "account export excludes internal Export blobs and attachments from the exported zip" do
    account = accounts("37s")

    first_export = account.exports.create!(user: admin)
    first_export.build_now

end

    # First import: signed in as kevin (already an admin in the exported account)
    import_1 = Account::Import.start(
      identity: kevin.identity,
      file: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(zip_path, "application/zip")
    )
    perform_enqueued_jobs
    import_1.reload
    assert import_1.completed?
    account_1 = import_1.account

    assert_equal source_account.users.count, account_1.users.count
    assert_equal 45.days.to_i, account_1.entropy.auto_postpone_period

    board_1 = account_1.boards.find_by!(name: "Writebook")
    assert board_1.published?
    assert_not_equal board.publication.key, board_1.publication.key

    card_1 = account_1.cards.find_by!(number: card.number)
    assert card_1.golden?
    assert_equal [ "First checklist step", "Second checklist step" ], card_1.steps.map(&:content)
    assert_includes card_1.reactions.map(&:content), "👍"

    # Second import of the exact same zip: signed in as david (was a member in exported account -> promoted to admin)
    import_2 = Account::Import.start(
      identity: david.identity,
      file: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(zip_path, "application/zip")
    )
    perform_enqueued_jobs
    import_2.reload
    assert import_2.completed?
    account_2 = import_2.account

    assert_not_equal account_1.id, account_2.id
    assert_equal source_account.users.count, account_2.users.count
    david_in_account_2 = account_2.users.find_by!(identity: david.identity)
    assert david_in_account_2.admin?

    board_2 = account_2.boards.find_by!(name: "Writebook")
    assert board_2.published?
    assert_not_equal board_1.publication.key, board_2.publication.key
  end

  test "cleanup removes stale finished imports and keeps pending or recent ones" do
    recent = Account::Import.create!(identity: identities(:kevin), status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
    stale_completed = Account::Import.create!(identity: identities(:kevin), status: :completed, completed_at: 2.days.ago)
    stale_completed.update_column(:updated_at, 2.days.ago)
    stale_failed = Account::Import.create!(identity: identities(:kevin), status: :failed, failure_reason: "Bad zip")
    stale_failed.update_column(:updated_at, 2.days.ago)
    in_progress = Account::Import.create!(identity: identities(:kevin), status: :processing)
    in_progress.update_column(:updated_at, 2.days.ago)

    Account::Import.cleanup

    assert Account::Import.exists?(recent.id)
    assert Account::Import.exists?(in_progress.id)
    assert_not Account::Import.exists?(stale_completed.id)
    assert_not Account::Import.exists?(stale_failed.id)
  end
end

Data export and import have been implemented across Fizzy:

- **Whole Account Export (`/account/settings` -> `POST /account/exports`, `GET /account/exports/:id`)**:
  - Admins see an **Export data** section in Account Settings to generate a single `.zip` archive of the entire account asynchronously (`Account::Export` / `Export::BuildJob`).
  - Streams database records (`Account::DataTransfer::Manifest` and specialized `RecordSet` classes) and attached files (`ZipFile.create_for`) for both local Disk and S3 storage.
  - Sends an email (`ExportMailer#completed`) with a download link that works for 24 hours (`1.day`) and expires afterward (with scheduled cleanup via `Export.cleanup`).

- **User Card Export (`users#show` -> `POST /users/:user_id/data_exports`, `GET /users/:user_id/data_exports/:id`)**:
  - Any user can export the published cards they have access to from their own profile page (`User::DataExport`).
  - Exports each accessible card as JSON (`{number}.json`) including its comments, plus every attached image and embedded file on the card and its comments (`{number}/{filename}`).
  - Sends an email (`ExportMailer#completed`) with a 24-hour download link.

- **Account Import (`GET /account/imports/new`, `POST /account/imports`, `GET /account/imports/:id`)**:
  - Any signed-in user can upload an account archive at `/account/imports/new` (`Account::Import` / `Account::ImportJob`).
  - Validates archive integrity upfront (`ZipFile.read_from` supporting both Disk and S3 HTTP Range streaming via `ZipFile::RemoteIO` / `ZipFile::Reader`), imports all boards, columns, cards, comments, steps, tags, filters, files/blobs, rich-text attachments/mentions, and people into a new account with deterministic UUIDv7 remapping, reindexes search, and reconciles storage totals.
  - Sends a completion email (`ImportMailer#completed`) with a link to the new account, or a failure email (`ImportMailer#failed`) explaining why the import failed while rolling back all database records and deleting any uploaded blobs/files so nothing is left behind.
